history.headline: Start day is here. The taper held and the engine is banked. From tomorrow the 580 km trail becomes the only data that matters.
watch_items: Watch how easy-day HR recalibrates once the pack and consecutive loaded days stack — the first few days will reset your sense of what steady costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load, not the engine, is the genuine unknown.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, distinct from the flatter coastal sections.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.

history.headline: Day one of the 580 km crossing. The taper landed clean and the engine is banked. From here the trail is the only data that counts.
watch_items: Watch how easy-effort HR recalibrates over the first loaded days — the pack and consecutive terrain will reset your sense of what steady costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability, not the aerobic engine, is the genuine unknown here.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, distinct from the flatter coastal sections.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.

history.headline: The logged data stops before the crossing you're apparently mid-way through. Nothing from the trail has landed here yet. Until it does, this reads as a clean post-taper baseline, not a race in progress.
watch_items: The obvious one: whether the crossing sessions actually appear in the feed — right now there's a gap between the narrative and the logged data, and the trail is the only evidence that counts.
Once trail data arrives, watch the cardio-load status flip out of its false "detraining" reading — the speed of that reversal will tell you how hard the first days loaded you.
Keep an eye on whether nightly recovery consolidates as trail rhythm replaces the logistics window, since the recent nights are still choppy.

history.headline: The first big trail effort has landed — a long, low-HR day on foot at controlled intensity. This is durability work, not a race pace. The gap between narrative and data has closed.
watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status reverses out of its detraining reading once the long effort registers — the speed of that flip is a fair proxy for how hard this day loaded you.
Watch how the day or two after the long effort look: whether easy-run HR sits normal or runs elevated, which will tell you how much the effort actually cost.
Watch whether nightly recovery consolidates now that the logistics-heavy window is passing, since the recent nights are still short and broken.
Watch for any back-to-back long efforts appearing — that's the durability quality this block is genuinely training, and worth confirming in the data.

history.headline: Back-to-back ultra-distance days on foot at controlled HR — the durability quality this block trains, confirmed in the clearest terms yet. The engine held its shape across both. Recovery is now the story.
watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status flips out of detraining now that both long days are logged — a slow flip signals a heavier real cost than the low HR implied.
Watch the first few easy runs after the crossing for elevated HR at normal pace, which would show the effort is still being paid down.
Watch whether nightly sleep consolidates now that the crossing window is closing, since recent nights have been short and fragmented.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return is a fair marker that the trail block has been absorbed and normal training rhythm has resumed.
